profile.university: University of North Carolina at Charlotte
bio: I am an Assistant Professor in the Department of Computer Science at UNC Charlotte, where I lead the High-Performance Data Intensive (HPDi) Lab. My research focuses on high-performance computing and scientific data management, with an emphasis on data reduction, compression, and parallel and distributed systems.

I received my Ph.D. from the New Jersey Institute of Technology, advised by Qing Liu, and my bachelor's degree from Shandong University. I was a research intern at Los Alamos National Laboratory from 2022 to 2023. I am also affiliated with the High Performance Computing and Systems Lab at UNC Charlotte.

projects.name: Compression Quality Prediction
projects.subtitle: DeepCQ and QualityNet
projects.description: We develop deep surrogate models that estimate the quality of scientific lossy compression and support informed configuration choices. QualityNet studies error-bounded compression quality prediction. DeepCQ extends this direction with a modular two-stage framework that reuses extracted features across compressors, quality metrics, and scientific datasets.

lab.mission: HPDi Lab is led by Jinzhen Wang in the Department of Computer Science at the University of North Carolina at Charlotte. We study high-performance computing and scientific data management, developing efficient methods for data reduction, compression, and data access in parallel and distributed systems. Our research combines system design, performance modeling, and machine learning to manage large scientific datasets and guide compression decisions. Our mission is to reduce the cost of storing, moving, and processing scientific data while preserving the information needed for analysis and discovery.

bio: I am an Assistant Professor of Computer Science at UNC Charlotte, leading the High-Performance Data Intensive (HPDi) Lab. My research focuses on high-performance computing and scientific data management, especially data reduction, compression, and parallel and distributed systems.

I earned my Ph.D. at NJIT with Qing Liu and my bachelor's degree at Shandong University. I interned at Los Alamos National Laboratory (2022–2023) and am affiliated with Charlotte's High Performance Computing and Systems Lab.

projects.deepcq: A two-stage deep-surrogate framework for predicting lossy compression quality. Reusable features support configuration selection across compressors, metrics, and scientific datasets without a full compression sweep.
projects.qualitynet: Fast surrogate models estimate compression quality to guide configuration choices for scientific datasets.
projects.genesis: Phase I research in the first DOE Genesis Mission cohort, connecting artificial intelligence and scientific computing.
